rules.statement: Express a security profile's constraints as settings combined with commutative, idempotent merge operations (Intersect for allowed-value ceilings, Or for requirement floors, Min for lifetime ceilings), so a more specific scope in the settings cascade cannot loosen them.
rules.why: Because these operations are commutative and idempotent, it doesn't matter where a constraint enters the cascade, and a child tenant or client can never weaken a constraint its parent mandated.
rules.check: Look for profile or policy constraints applied with child-overrides-parent or last-wins merges, or written as separate imperative checks that a child scope's setting can override.

rules.statement: Have discovery metadata and request-time enforcement read the same effective settings, not keep a separate copy of a profile's constraints for either one.
rules.why: With one source of truth, the advertised metadata and the enforced behavior cannot drift apart.
rules.check: Look for discovery documents built from hard-coded or duplicated values instead of the effective settings that the endpoints use to validate requests, or the reverse.

rules.statement: Route every load path for persisted scope settings (initial load, refresh and per-client resolution) through a single entry point that both deserializes the settings and applies any selected security profiles.
rules.why: With a single entry point, no load path can skip the profile and quietly run with loosened settings.
rules.check: Look for new or changed code that deserializes tenant or client settings directly without going through the shared deserialize-and-expand call.

rules.statement: Under the FAPI 2.0 profile, limit signing algorithms to PS256, ES256 and Ed25519 (never the polymorphic EdDSA), client authentication to private_key_jwt, tls_client_auth and self_signed_tls_client_auth, response_type to code, and PKCE to S256; require PKCE and PAR; and cap authorization-code lifetime at 60 seconds and PAR request_uri lifetime at 90 seconds.
rules.why: These are the constraints the FAPI 2.0 Security Profile requires, so the OP can be configured to conform with a single switch.
rules.check: Check any change to the FAPI profile definition for permitted values or limits that are looser than these (for example client_secret_* or none auth, EdDSA, plain PKCE, or longer lifetimes).

rules.statement: At the token endpoint, reject a client authentication whose method is not allowed by the client's effective token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported ceiling, and treat an empty ceiling as permitting no method.
rules.why: Enforcing the permitted methods makes the profile's client-authentication ceiling take effect: under FAPI 2.0 it rejects weak (client_secret_*) and public (none) authentication, and the amended decision says an empty ceiling permits nothing.
rules.check: Look for client authentication that accepts any method a handler can validate without checking it against the effective permitted set, or that treats an empty permitted set as unrestricted.
